result.instructions: Use the lsp_* tools for semantic code questions: where a symbol is defined, who calls it, its type, or what the compiler complains about. They are type-aware and cross-file, so they beat grep for names, types and call relationships. Target symbols by name ("parse_config"), not line:column. lsp_status shows which servers run and what they are doing. If a result starts with [indexing] the server is still indexing: wait a few seconds and retry instead of concluding the symbol does not exist. All tools are read-only.

tools.description: Report the language servers running for this workspace: version, pid, uptime, memory, connected clients, and each instance's state and indexing progress. Call it before blaming the tools — it separates "no server is running" from "the server is still indexing", which grep can never tell you. Example: lsp_status(). When a server shows [indexing], wait a few seconds and retry rather than giving up on LSP.
tools.name: lsp_status

tools.description: Find symbols by name across the workspace with a type-aware index. Better than grep because it matches declarations, not text: a comment or a string containing the name is not a hit, and each result carries file, line and kind. Example: lsp_find_symbol(query="parse"). If you get [indexing], retry in a few seconds. If you get [language_disabled], that language was not enabled for this connection; do not retry — use another tool.

language.description: Restrict to one enabled language, e.g. `rust`, `go`.

limit.description: Most symbols to list; default 50, maximum 200.

path.description: A file or directory that scopes the answer to what is inside it.

query.description: Name to search for; fuzzy, so `parse` also finds `parse_args`.

tools.name: lsp_find_symbol

tools.description: Jump from a symbol to where it is defined, following the import that grep cannot: grep finds every file mentioning the name, the server finds the one this use means. Example: lsp_definition(symbol="LspConfig") — prefer symbol over path+line+column, you should not have to count characters. If the answer is [indexing], retry in a few seconds.

column.description: 1-based character on that line; give it with line, not with symbol.

line.description: 1-based line; give it with column, and not with symbol.

path.description: File to look in; with line and column it is the position.

symbol.description: Symbol name; may be qualified, e.g. `Foo::bar` or `pkg.Foo`.

tools.name: lsp_definition

tools.description: List every use of a symbol, grouped by file, as only the compiler can: comments and strings are excluded, and uses across files and crates are found. This is the tool to reach for instead of grep before a rename or a deletion. Example: lsp_references(symbol="LspConfig::new"). If the answer is [indexing], retry shortly.

column.description: 1-based character on that line; give it with line, not with symbol.

include_declaration.description: Also list the declaration itself; default false.

line.description: 1-based line; give it with column, and not with symbol.

path.description: File to look in; with line and column it is the position.

symbol.description: Symbol name; may be qualified, e.g. `Foo::bar` or `pkg.Foo`.

tools.name: lsp_references

tools.description: Show the type and documentation of a symbol — the compiler's view, not the raw text grep would return: resolved signature, parameter types, doc comment. Example: lsp_hover(symbol="Config::load"). If you get [indexing], wait a few seconds and retry.

column.description: 1-based character on that line; give it with line, not with symbol.

line.description: 1-based line; give it with column, and not with symbol.

path.description: File to look in; with line and column it is the position.

symbol.description: Symbol name; may be qualified, e.g. `Foo::bar` or `pkg.Foo`.

tools.name: lsp_hover

tools.description: Find the types that implement a trait or interface, or the methods that override one. grep cannot answer this: the spelling differs per language and the answer crosses files. Example: lsp_implementations(symbol="LspBackend"). If you get [indexing], retry in a few seconds.

column.description: 1-based character on that line; give it with line, not with symbol.

line.description: 1-based line; give it with column, and not with symbol.

path.description: File to look in; with line and column it is the position.

symbol.description: Symbol name; may be qualified, e.g. `Foo::bar` or `pkg.Foo`.

tools.name: lsp_implementations

tools.description: List the symbols a file declares, nested by scope, with kinds and line numbers. Cheaper than reading the file and more accurate than grepping `fn`/`func`/`def`: it is the language's own parse tree. Example: lsp_outline(path="src/lib.rs"). If you get [indexing], retry in a few seconds.

path.description: File to outline, absolute or relative to the workspace root.

tools.name: lsp_outline

tools.description: List the functions that call this one, as an indented tree — the question grep answers badly, since a comment naming it is not a caller. Follows `depth` levels up (1-3; default 1); each line is `name  path:line:column`, and a place already shown says `(see above)`. Use it before changing a signature. Example: lsp_callers(symbol="LspConfig::new"). If you get [indexing], retry in a few seconds.

column.description: 1-based character on that line; give it with line, not with symbol.

depth.description: How many levels to follow, 1 to 3; default 1.

line.description: 1-based line; give it with column, and not with symbol.

path.description: File to look in; with line and column it is the position.

symbol.description: Symbol name; may be qualified, e.g. `Foo::bar` or `pkg.Foo`.

tools.name: lsp_callers

tools.description: List the functions this one calls, as the language server resolved them and as an indented tree — calls, not the text grep would return. Follows `depth` levels down (1-3; default 1); each line is `name  path:line:column`. Use it to see what a function touches before you change it. Example: lsp_callees(symbol="main"). If you get [indexing], retry in a few seconds.

column.description: 1-based character on that line; give it with line, not with symbol.

depth.description: How many levels to follow, 1 to 3; default 1.

line.description: 1-based line; give it with column, and not with symbol.

path.description: File to look in; with line and column it is the position.

symbol.description: Symbol name; may be qualified, e.g. `Foo::bar` or `pkg.Foo`.

tools.name: lsp_callees

tools.description: Report the compiler and linter errors and warnings for a file, with line and column. Use it right after you edit a file to check it still compiles — the server's verdict, not your guess. Example: lsp_diagnostics(path="src/lib.rs"). If it says the diagnostics are not known yet, ask again instead of assuming the file is clean.

path.description: File to diagnose, absolute or relative to the workspace root.

tools.name: lsp_diagnostics

tools.description: Preview the whole-project edit for renaming a symbol, as a unified diff — nothing on disk changes. Better than grep+sed: exact references, no comments or strings, every affected file shown before you touch it. Example: lsp_rename_preview(symbol="LspConfig::new", new_name="build"). If you get [indexing], retry in a few seconds: a rename now could miss references.

column.description: 1-based character on that line; give it with line, not with symbol.

line.description: 1-based line; give it with column, and not with symbol.

new_name.description: The new name: one identifier, no spaces, at most 200 characters.

path.description: File to look in; with line and column it is the position.

symbol.description: Symbol name; may be qualified, e.g. `Foo::bar` or `pkg.Foo`.

tools.name: lsp_rename_preview
